stories.headline: WNBA playoff picture 2026: How will final seeds be set Thursday?
stories.summary: Before the playoffs open Sunday, the final four seeds will be set in Thursday's regular-season finales.
stories.body:
Four seeds are set for the 2026 WNBA playoffs, but the other four come down to Thursday, the last night of the regular season. Five games are on the schedule, and four have playoff implications.

The Minnesota Lynx are the No. 1 seed, secured Tuesday thanks to the Golden State Valkyries' loss at the Portland Fire.

The other seeds were set Wednesday after the Atlanta Dream's 83-65 win over the New York Liberty. That put the Dream into the No. 4 seed and the Liberty into No. 8, plus locked the Dallas Wings into No. 7.

Minnesota and New York will meet in the first round.

Here's how the remaining seeds and playoff matchups will be decided.

Nos. 2 and 3 seeds

Golden State and the defending champion Las Vegas Aces will host first-round games but are still jockeying for position.

On Thursday, the Valkyries (31-12) play at the Los Angeles Sparks, while the Aces (30-13) visit the Phoenix Mercury. Golden State will get the No. 2 seed with a victory or a Las Vegas loss.

But if Golden State loses and Las Vegas wins, both teams finish 31-13, and the Aces will be the No. 2 seed. They own the tiebreaker thanks to their 3-0 regular-season record against the Valkyries.

Nos. 5 and 6 seeds

This will come down to the Indiana Fever and the Washington Mystics.

Thursday, Indiana plays at Minnesota two days after the Fever's 96-77 win over the Lynx in Indianapolis on Tuesday. Lynx point guard Olivia Miles didn't play in that game because of a calf injury and has already been ruled out for Thursday.

With a victory, the Fever will get the No. 5 seed, as they will finish 29-15. However, if the Fever lose and Washington beats the Chicago Sky, the Fever and the Mystics would finish 28-16. In that case, Washington would be the No. 5 seed and Indiana No. 6 since the Mystics have the tiebreaker with their 2-1 regular-season series record against the Fever.

If the Fever end up at No. 6, that will be their third season in a row with that seed. The Mystics missed the playoffs the past two seasons.

Playoffs open Sunday

All four best-of-three first-round playoff series begin Sunday, starting on the home court of the higher seed. If the series goes to a deciding Game 3, the higher seed hosts that game, too.

"Little things matter in the playoffs, and that might be one of them," Atlanta's Naz Hillmon said Wednesday about the Dream being in the top four and having home-court advantage in the first round. "Just having that energy behind us from our fans."

stories.headline: Projecting the NHL's leap-forward, regression candidates
stories.summary: Here are a dozen players who are in for a heightened -- or lowered -- level of production this season.
stories.body:
Every year, fantasy hockey managers look for players who could see a massive jump in production to get value in later rounds. They are also keenly in tune with "buyer beware" situations on players coming off stupendous seasons.

Casual NHL fans want to understand reasonable expectations for developing young players, and drop-offs after great seasons. I've identified a dozen players who fall into one of those two categories for 2026-27.

To qualify for this list, a player cannot be a rookie. Many players projected to take a meaningful step forward are in their final years of their entry-level contracts or in the first year of their first standard contract. Many players projected to take a step back enjoyed career years in 2025-26, with elevated shooting percentages or roles they are unlikely to maintain.

How to watch the 2026-27 NHL season on ESPN networks -- including 100 exclusive games and the out-of-market package (over 1,050 games).

Leap forward candidates

Matvei Michkov, RW, Philadelphia Flyers
Age: 21 | Contract AAV: $950,000

2025-26 stats: 81 GP | 20 G | 31 A

I've been on the Michkov train for a very long time, and after what seems to be a very impressive summer, Michkov seems primed for a true breakout.

He is rightfully having to earn the trust of Rick Tocchet, but the Flyers absolutely need a more balanced offense to avoid a step back this season.

Michkov's talent is undeniable, and a summer in which he prepared his body for the grind of the NHL season should see him able to execute more effectively. At his best, Michkov can be a top-six difference-maker at even strength and a reliable power-play option. His production will directly relate to the opportunity he earns -- and is hopefully given.

There is every reason to be excited and every reason for the Flyers to reward their young talent with greater opportunity. If Tocchet gives him offensive opportunities and chances to show his development, Michkov could crack the point-per-game threshold and establish himself as a go-to offensive producer.

Matthew Wood, RW, Nashville Predators
Age: 21 | Contract AAV: $950,000

2025-26 stats: 71 GP | 17 G | 13 A

One of the key players of Nashville's rebuild enters his second season primed for a much bigger opportunity. Wood is expected to play regular top-six minutes with Filip Forsberg and get a long look on the top power-play unit.

Given Wood's physical makeup, he has the package to be a power forward with significant goal scoring potential. His net-front presence on the power play will be a nuisance to opposing goaltenders, and his ability to drive off the rush should pose problems for defenders.

Centering Forsberg provides Wood a great opportunity to produce offense and cement himself as a top-six center. Accounting for increased ice time, power-play opportunity and expected improvement of the team around him, Wood's production could reasonably rise to 55 points, nearly double his rookie season (30 points). He's not the only player who could break out in Nashville, but Wood seems to be the most reasonable bet to take a tangible leap in his offensive production given the opportunity.

Gabe Perreault, RW, New York Rangers
Age: 21 | Contract AAV: $941,667

2025-26 stats: 49 GP | 12 G | 15 A

Finding yourself on the top line to start the season is a recipe for a breakout. The Rangers seem poised to give their budding young star a real opportunity to become a bona fide offensive threat in his second NHL season.

The tremendously talented winger will see a sharp increase in ice time at even strength and might play his way onto the top power-play unit at various points through the season. His goal-scoring ability should suit Mika Zibanejad's playmaking ability, and the two of them should develop significant chemistry.

The Rangers desperately need their young players to contribute meaningful offense to make the best of what is left in the careers of Zibanejad, Adam Fox, Igor Shesterkin and J.T. Miller. Perreault is critical to that, and thus the opportunity presented to him is a recipe for breakout success. If Perreault plays top-line minutes and gets power-play time -- he's projected to score 23 goals and 60 points -- it will be a major step forward in his development.

Michael Misa, C, San Jose Sharks
Age: 19 | Contract AAV: $986,250

2025-26 stats: 45 GP | 9 G | 12 A

Misa might see the biggest jump in his production this season. Given the trajectory of San Jose and his development, there is a real chance the young Shark triples his rookie production. Misa enters his second season after putting on significant muscle, and training with fellow Sharks Macklin Celebrini and Sam Dickinson this summer.

It is highly likely that Misa takes over Alexander Wennberg's spot as the second-line center and becomes the primary weapon on the second power-play unit. In a 45-game rookie season, Misa tallied 21 points, nearly a half point per game.

There is every reason to believe that Misa could produce 65-plus points in a full season in which his ice time should increase by 20%. Misa's development should continue on defense as well, taking a major step to becoming a two-way play-driving center.

With development on both ends of the ice and increased opportunity, Misa's breakout season could be two-fold as he becomes one of the best young players to watch in the NHL.

Luke Evangelista, RW, New Jersey Devils
Age: 24 | Contract AAV: $3 million

2025-26 stats: 81 GP | 121 G | 44 A

One of the shrewdest acquisitions of the summer was made by the Devils. Evangelista will get significant offensive opportunity in New Jersey's top six, and given the left-handed offensive talent already on the roster, his right-handed shooting will bring some balance.

He's likely to get an extended opportunity on the top power-play unit because of Sheldon Keefe's desire for a right-handed shooter to complement the unit. Evangelista's style is going to create space and offensive opportunities for his linemates, by winning puck battles and getting pucks to scorers in dangerous areas.

He might take time to adjust to the offensive system in Jersey, meaning the points might not come right away. But he's highly underrated as a two-way player that makes him the perfect fit beside Nico Hischier and certainly will be relied upon in key situations on both ends of the ice, providing value as he finds his offensive step. Evangelista's step forward should not only see a step forward in production but some recognition as one of the league's quality defensive wingers.

Jimmy Snuggerud, RW, St. Louis Blues
Age: 22 | Contract AAV: $950,000

2025-26 stats: 70 GP | 21 G | 30 A

Snuggerud finds himself on the right wing of what has the potential to be one of the best lines in the NHL, this season. Paired with Dylan Holloway and Robert Thomas, Snuggerud will be the beneficiary of Holloway's speed and successful puck retrievals and battles, as well as Thomas' playmaking ability. Snuggerud is a perfect fit to play with those two and it is more than conceivable that he capitalizes on the opportunity by scoring more than 30 goals.

Snuggerud had a wonderful rookie season and given his trajectory and his quality of teammate, he's going to be one of the go-to scoring threats for the Blues for the foreseeable future. With a step forward in development, Snuggerud should also help a power play that struggled last season, and easily top his five power-play goals in 2025-26.

This combination of factors should see Snuggerud cement himself as a top-line offensive threat capable of producing 80-plus points.

Honorable mention

Nicholas Robertson, LW, Pittsburgh Penguins
Age: 25 | Contract AAV: $3.25 million

2025-26 stats: 78 GP | 16 G | 16 A

He's playing next to Sidney Crosby. For as long as that happens, it is reasonable to assume that his production would be leaps and bounds better than previous seasons. The list of players whose production rose astronomically after finding chemistry with Crosby is long. There is no need to read into it more than that.

Regression candidates

Anthony Mantha, RW, New Jersey Devils
Age: 32 | Contract AAV: $4.75 million

2025-26 stats: 81 GP | 33 G | 31 A

The last time Mantha had a season with more than 20 goals, the world did not know about COVID-19. So yes, it has been a while.

Mantha is coming off a 33-31-64 season, far surpassing his career highs. Last season was the second of Mantha's career in which he played 80 or more games; he has struggled to stay healthy. The interesting part about Mantha is that he has enjoyed three consecutive seasons with a shooting percentage over 20%. Though that might not be his true shooting talent, he has sustained it for a large enough sample size that it is reasonable to assume he is an elite shooter.

This season, Mantha will be afforded the opportunity to play in New Jersey's top six, centered by one of Jack Hughes or Nico Hischier. His placement on this list is largely due to his projection of playing only 71 games this season. He's going to get less power-play time than he did last season, because the Devils' top unit plays a significant portion of the power play, and an output of seven power-play goals is highly unlikely to sustain.

There's a very likely situation that Mantha's shooting percentage remains high, but his production falls to about 50 points, which would be around a 20% regression.

Pavel Zacha, C, Boston Bruins
Age: 29 | Contract AAV: $4.75 million

2025-26 stats: 78 GP | 30 G | 35 A

Coming off a career season, in which his goal total was nearly 50% better than his previous high, Zacha is highly likely to see a return to his 20-goal norm. Hitting the 30-goal mark was buoyed by a shooting percentage of 22.9%, one of the highest in the NHL last season and 6.4 percentage points higher than his previous career-high shooting percentage of 16.5%.

My model projects him to score 23 goals if he retains the second-line role for Boston. If he is surpassed by Fraser Minten, it falls to 20. Moreover, Boston is expected to be in a tougher spot this season with the improvements of Buffalo and Montreal, and the expected return to competitiveness of Florida and Toronto. The games that Zacha plays will be tighter, given the strength of the Atlantic Division.

Of the regression candidates, Zacha is most likely to see the biggest step back given the combination of shooting luck and expected role.

Darren Raddysh, D, Toronto Maple Leafs
Age: 30 | Contract AAV: $8.5 million

2025-26 stats: 73 GP | 22 G | 48 A

Raddysh is going to have the basically the same offensive opportunity in Toronto that he was afforded last season in Tampa Bay. He will run the top power-play unit and be depended on to play top-pair minutes and generate offense from the back end. Expecting Raddysh to produce near a point-per-game pace is wholly unreasonable.

Raddysh performed at his best with a strong defensive partner that allowed him to take risks and drive play. With the Leafs, a healthy Chris Tanev or Jake McCabe would be the closest to replicating the partnership he had in Tampa Bay. Without that, Raddysh's defensive load would increase, which will depress his offensive involvement and production.

Furthermore, Raddysh benefitted from one of the best power-play players of the generation in Nikita Kucherov. The Leafs do not have a dual threat of that level. Auston Matthews and William Nylander are primary shooters, but neither is the dual-threat passer and shooter that Kucherov is, making them more predictable. Raddysh will play with extraordinarily talented players in Toronto, but equaling his career-high point total (after doubling it from the previous season) is rarely sustainable for nonsuperstar players.

Reasonable expectations would have Raddysh in the midteens for goals and high 50s in total points. Though that's still among the game's best, it is a significant step back from a near point-per-game season in 2025-26.

Nick Schmaltz, C, Utah Mammoth
Age: 30 | Contract AAV: $8 million

2025-26 stats: 82 GP | 33 G | 41 A

Schmaltz is coming off a career season in which he scored 33 goals and 74 points, a 44% increase in goal-scoring output over his previous career high of 23. When healthy, Schmaltz is a true talent 25-27 goal scorer.

Heading into this season, Schmaltz is going to battle a few forces against him. His shooting percentage and regression to his true talent is likely to lead to a drop into the 60s in points. More importantly, Logan Cooley could ascend to the top-line center role in Utah in 2026-27. Combine that with the addition of Vincent Trocheck in the offseason, and Schmaltz is likely to see a reduction in ice time by 2½ to 3 minutes per game from his 2025-26 average of 19:43.

Utah's center depth took a meaningful step forward with the Trocheck acquisition, and should balance how the top lines are deployed. The combination of each of these factors is likely to lead to a 15% reduction in offensive production, with a projected total of 26 goals and 63 points.

Wyatt Johnston, C, Dallas Stars
Age: 23 | Contract AAV: $8.4 million

2025-26 stats: 82 GP | 45 G | 41 A

The Stars might take a step back as a whole this season. Whether they do or don't, the likelihood of Johnston scoring 27 power-play goals again is low.

Johnston is an excellent player and the drop-off in power-play production is not an indictment of him as a player. It's more that those types of power-play numbers are generally not repeatable by the game's elite. For reference, Alex Ovechkin's career high is 25 power-play goals and he is the greatest goal scorer in the history of the sport. He topped Johnston's 42 power-play points twice in his 21-year career. The notion that Johnston would be able to outpace the game's greatest goal scorer on the power play is not one based in reality.

Johnston's play and value to the Stars is unlikely to regress given his age and talent, but his production rate is likely to regress. Forty-two of Johnston's 86 points in 2025-26 came on the power play, where a more sustainable output would see Johnston notch 30 power-play points.

Beyond the power play, a shooting percentage of 21.8% is likely to regress to 17%, seeing Johnston's goal total dropping to the mid-30s. Combine those factors and a healthy Roope Hintz to carry some of the offensive load, it is conceivable that Johnston's production suffers a 12% drop-off, roughly 11 points.

stories.headline: Azerbaijan GP: George Russell fastest in first practice; Kimi Antonelli suffers mechanical issue
stories.summary: George Russell got his Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend off to a good start after he topped first practice, while his teammate Kimi Antonelli was forced to end his session early.
stories.body:
George Russell got his Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend off to a good start after he topped first practice, while his teammate Kimi Antonelli was forced to end his session early.

The Mercedes driver set a time of 1:45.387, four-tenths quicker than Red Bull's Max Verstappen around the streets of Baku.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished in third, while his teammate Lewis Hamilton sat behind in fourth.

Antonelli ended the session in fifth, eight-tenths off Russell's pace, before he had to stop on the track after reporting a hydraulic failure on his Mercedes.

Near the halfway point of the session, the young Italian, who is leading the world championship by 81 points to Russell, completed only nine laps before suffering the issue.

Carlos Sainz in the heavily-upgraded Williams had a brake fire issue in the pit lane which was put out quickly in the first half of the session.

Other teams which have brought major upgrades this weekend are McLaren and Red Bull, and while Verstappen was looking strong, McLaren spent a lot of the session working on the cars in both sides of the garage.

- Alpine's Pierre Gasly warns against 'disturbing' threats after teammate Franco Colapinto incident

- Lewis Hamilton 'hopes' F1 will race in the Middle East despite ongoing conflict

- Why is the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on a Saturday, not a Sunday? Baku schedule shift explained

Oscar Piastri was reporting on the McLaren team radio that he was experiencing vibrations early on and was sent back to the garage later in the session. The Australian finished sixth overall, over one second off the leader's pace.

His teammate Lando Norris didn't get much running and finished down in 14th.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad finished seventh and eighth.

The second practice session will get going at 1 p.m. UK / 8 a.m. ET.

stories.headline: Lachie Neale ban overturned, free to play AFL Grand Final
stories.summary: Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL grand final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.
stories.body:
Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL Grand Final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.

The dual Brownlow Medal winner will feature in the premiership decider against Fremantle - his former club - at the MCG on Saturday after having a striking charge on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan downgraded on Thursday.

Neale will instead be fined $10,000.

He initially failed in challenging the one-game ban from the match review officer at the tribunal on Tuesday night.

To succeed on appeal, Brisbane had to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

The Lons were able to sway the appeals board that the tribunal had made an error of law in not considering the exceptional and compelling circumstances of Neale not having previously been suspended in 320 AFL games.

Neale avoids becoming the first player to miss an AFL grand final following a preliminary-final suspension since Collingwood's Anthony Rocca in 2003.

Brisbane legal representative Adrian Anderson tried various different arguments to clear Neale.

One included suggesting the ban should be served in round one next year, instead of in the grand final, due to the added importance of the match.

It was a bold strategy given Neale is almost certain to leave Brisbane and join Collingwood during the off-season.

Anderson leaned heavily on Neale's prior record of not being suspended, referring to the four-time All-Australian as "pretty close to a unicorn".

Introduced this year, the "exceptional and compelling circumstances" clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and AFL games record-holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

New vision of Neale's strike on Ginnivan became available on Thursday, but was not allowed to be used because it was not shown at Tuesday's tribunal hearing.

The footage would have shown a clearer picture of the incident and likely not helped Neale's case.

Sydney's Barry Hall (2005) and Richmond's Trent Cotchin (2017) famously escaped bans for incidents in their respective preliminary finals to play in eventual premiership wins.

The Lions named Neale in their team on Thursday, shortly before the decision was handed down, and didn't need to change the 23.

With rain expected for Saturday's grand final, Neale will figure prominently as one of the Lions' best wet-weather players.

stories.headline: Is Sullivan the next Olise? Comparisons for USMNT's top young stars
stories.summary: With the USMNT welcoming a new class of debutantes during this international break, ESPN dives into the numbers of the United States' next prodigies.
stories.body:
If one word defines the first call-up for the U.S. men's national team since the summer's FIFA World Cup, it's this: youth.

To give the next generation some opportunities, coach Mauricio Pochettino has given several key figures a break and instead selected a noticeably younger group for upcoming friendlies in late September and early October.

Of the 28 chosen, 13 have yet to make their senior national team debut. From those 13, eight are teenagers who are continuing to fine-tune and develop their talents.

Though some of these players are literally still kids, they also represent an exciting generation of up-and-comers who have the potential to become elite game changers for the U.S. by the time the 2030 World Cup rolls around, if not sooner.

Shining a light on a few of these fresh faces, we've selected five names to follow in the upcoming international break. We've also enlisted the help of ESPN's in-house guru Bill Connelly, who has provided key stats (over the last 365 days in all competitions) on each name, as well as both overly optimistic and realistic comparisons to players that they could one day become.

Zavier Gozo | Midfielder | 19 | Crystal Palace

Within just three years, Gozo went from earning his MLS debut in 2023 with Real Salt Lake to then gaining a high-profile move to the Premier League this summer with Crystal Palace.

Typically playing on the right flank, the 19-year-old midfielder has an immense amount of energy with 8.1 progressive carries per 90 minutes. In fact, even though Gozo hasn't played in MLS since July -- before his move to the Premier League -- he still ranks second overall in MLS for total progressive carries, carries following a defensive action, and take-ons, among teenagers in MLS.

"He is insanely robust. If I were to tell you the running numbers he's putting up, they're, for his age, I think world-class," said Nate Miller, a former assistant at Real Salt Lake, to ESPN.

With six goals and five assists across 1,614 minutes in the last year, the attack-minded midfielder has stepped up with his 3.1 shots per 90 minutes. He is also crucial in regaining the ball thanks to his 6.8 defensive interventions per 90 minutes. Looking back at teenagers within MLS, Gozo is still second in 2026 when it comes to total tackles.

"We don't know who's going to come through," said Miller about the next generation of U.S. stars. "But he should be one of the main guys in the national team in the future."

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Barcelona and Spain's Lamine Yamal

More realistic comparison: Leeds United's Brenden Aaronson

Mathis Albert | Midfielder | 17 | Borussia Dortmund

When Albert stepped onto the pitch in April for German side Borussia Dortmund, the midfielder made history as the youngest American to play in the Bundesliga at the age of 16. Since then, his appearances have been limited as a backup option on the bench --- which will skew some of our stats --- but the midfielder remains an intriguing option for the future of the national team.

Across all competitions, the former LA Galaxy academy player is averaging 8.3 progressive carries, 3.3 shots and 11.9 ground duels per 90 minutes.

"He was fearless, he was brave, he was relentless," said U.S. youth national team coach Gonzalo Segares to Goal.com about Albert.

"What stood out was his one-on-one ability. That's something we look at in players: being comfortable to take on players and beat them. That's a special talent that we look for in attacking players, and he had it."

When watching clips of the player, his pace, dribbling and tenacity (typically on the left wing) immediately shine. During his last appearance for Dortmund earlier this month, the South Carolina native led his team in shots, dribbles and ground duels in a 5-0 victory over HEBC Hamburg in the German Cup.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: PSG and Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia

More realistic comparison: Real Betis and Morocco's Abde Ezzalzouli

Cavan Sullivan | Midfielder | 16 | Philadelphia Union

There is no young American player gaining more hype or attention than the Manchester City-bound Sullivan. Set to join the Premier League giants when he turns 18, the attacking midfielder has kept pace with the likes of Lionel Messi since MLS returned to play after the World Cup.

The league leaders in goal contributions after the summer break? That's Sullivan and Messi with 13 apiece.

"A lot of attention goes on the creative things that he brings to the game," said interim head coach Ryan Richter to ESPN. "But the thing that stands out to me the most is his mentality and his competitiveness and the way that he approaches every single day."

In MLS, Sullivan is averaging 1.10 goals+assists, 2.4 chances and 2.9 shots per 90 minutes. More than just a dynamic chance-creator, improving finisher, and scrappy recoverer of the ball, there's an undeniable level of confidence in a player that makes clever on-the-field decisions that's far beyond his years. He is also incredibly fun to watch with his technical flair that's on display, as seen with this backheel goal this month.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Bayern Munich and France's Michael Olise

More realistic comparison: Arsenal and Greece's Christos Tzolis

Julian Hall | Forward | 18 | Red Bull New York

The highest-scoring teenager in MLS this season? That plaudit belongs to Red Bull New York forward Hall, who leads the 16-19 age group with a total of 10 goals across 26 appearances.

Efficiency comes to mind for the player who has 51% of his shots hitting the target, which ranks him seventh across MLS when analyzing those who have at least 10 goals this season.

Across all competitions, Hall has 18 goal contributions across 2,448 minutes in the past year, an average of 2.3 shots per 90 minutes, and is noticeably focused on close-range opportunities with 82.3% of shots emerging from inside the 18-yard box. In his first start of the 2026 season, the striker also gained plenty of attention after scoring twice for his club in a 2-1 victory.

"What stands out to me with Julian is his mentality," coach Michael Bradley said to ESPN.

"Obviously, the speed, the ability to change a game, the ability to get behind defenders and make things happen, those things are clear. He has a real belief in himself. He's willing to listen, he wants to learn, and he's constantly trying to understand how he can get better. You see that in the way he works every day."

Smart with his movement and runs, as well as a decent short passing game in the final third, expect him to be a possible difference-maker in the upcoming international window.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Atlético Madrid and Canada's Jonathan David

More realistic comparison: Borussia Dortmund and Portugal's Fábio Silva

Adri Mehmeti | Midfielder | 17 | Red Bull New York

While Hall is scoring goals, his teammate Mehmeti is doing plenty of the supporting work in the heart of the Red Bull starting XI.

With 6.6 ball recoveries per 90 minutes, the 17-year-old not only leads his team in recoveries but also the entire league in 2026. Thanks to his 77.9 touches and 9.0 line-breaking passes per 90 minutes, Mehmeti is also the league leader for touches and through balls among teenagers this season. Able to win the ball back and create opportunities going forward, Mehmeti impacts the defense and attack in any given match.

"For Adri, I think it's about continuing to develop the physical side and the defensive side of his game while maintaining the qualities that make him special with the ball," Bradley said to ESPN.

"He's playing a lot of minutes and taking on more responsibility, so now the challenge is learning how to manage a game for 90 minutes and understanding when to take risks, when to keep the ball, when to play forward and when to help the team breathe."

With friendlies against the likes of Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada coming up, we'll see if he can maintain that unfazed calm in his first call-up with the national team.

Way-too-optimistic comparison: Manchester City and England's Elliot Anderson

More realistic comparison: Internazionale and England's Curtis Jones

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Fiorot.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

stories.headline: Columbus Crew 2 fires Higuain after fallout from ref abuse
stories.summary: The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.
stories.body:
The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.

"We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuaín from his responsibilities," said Crew General Manager Issa Tall in prepared statement. "After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met," The Crew's statement added that for the 2026 MLS NEXT Pro Playoffs, the Crew 2 technical staff will assume additional responsibilities ahead of the Club's search for a full-time head coach for the side.

Higuain, 41, was suspended for two games following an Aug. 23 incident that involved him refusing to let go of the hand of a female referee during the post-game handshake, despite being asked three times to do so. Higuain also directed a sexist remark toward the referee saying: "Don't forget that this is a man's game."

Higuain, who excelled as a player for the Crew over eight seasons, was red carded for the incident. In addition to the two-game suspension, Higuain was ordered to undergo restorative practice training, sources told ESPN.

An MLS NEXT Pro spokesperson confirmed that Higuain was suspended for just one additional game, as the policy allows for the red card to count towards the total suspension. The same spokesperson wasn't able to answer the question of why Higuain's actions didn't constitute a forceful grab.

The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), the union that represents MLS and USL referees, brought the incident to light over the weekend, stating in a social media post that it was not satisfied with the penalties, adding that a "forceful grab" plus the discriminatory language should have been penalized more severely.

While the PSRA's post didn't mention Higuain by name, ESPN reported that the coach in question was Higuain.

"The League's response falls drastically short of the right message to the participants, the referees, and the public. It needs to be reevaluated," the PSRA's social media post read.

The Crew initially issued a statement stating that, "The Crew actively collaborated with MLS NEXT Pro throughout the review process and fully accepted the additional discipline issued in accordance with league policies.

"We condemn any action or notion that contradicts our mission of uniting and uplifting all communities and genders through the global game."

But sources with knowledge of the Crew's decision to fire its coach told ESPN that the club wasn't satisfied with Higuain's response to the incident, saying there was a "lack of contrition" on his part, that he refused to issue a public apology to the female referee, and that there was an overall lack of accountability on the part of its second-team coach.

There was pressure from several of the Crew's supporters groups as well, including the Nordecke and CapyBrava, which both made social media posts demanding that Higuain be fired.

One source said that Higuain was informed of the club's decision early Tuesday afternoon.

In a statement given to ESPN on Sunday, MLS NEXT Pro said the league "immediately investigated the reported incident between the head coach and the female official. It was determined that the coach's behavior violated League policies and warranted additional discipline beyond the red card that was issued in the moment. He served a two-game suspension and is required to participate in a multi-session restorative practices process, which is already underway. The program is intended to support the League's efforts to foster understanding, accountability, respect, and the restoration of relationships across the League. MLS NEXT Pro believes in the restorative approach. The League is confident in its process and the results."

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Selwyn Cobbo named Queensland's best for State of Origin
stories.summary: Queensland winger Selwyn Cobbo justified his State of Origin recall by winning the Ron McAuliffe Medal at the QRL awards night.
stories.body:
Dolphins winger Selwyn Cobbo received a boost ahead of the NRL preliminary final after winning Queensland's best player award for the State of Origin series.

The 24-year-old scored four tries, made four line breaks and averaged a stunning 184m across the three matches of 2-1 series loss. He was recalled by coach Billy Slater after a two-year absence from the Origin arena, due to the stellar club form he has displayed for the Dolphins.

Cobbo was a worthy winner of the Ron McAuliffe Medal, named in honour of the former senator and influential boss of the Queensland Rugby League.

Cobbo will play against the Sydney Roosters in the grand final qualifier on Friday night.

He won the Queensland gong at the QRL season awards on Thursday night in Brisbane, 17 years after Maroons legend Greg Inglis, who was his idol growing up.

Maroons prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui took out the FOGS Peter Jackson Memorial Award after his brave and emotional display in game two in Melbourne, where he played his heart out just days after his father Fereti Fa'asuamaleaui had died.

The Maroons won the match 44-24.

The award, named in honour of late Queensland star Jackson, is presented to a Maroons player or one of the support staff who epitomises what the Queensland Origin spirit is all about

Cobbo moved to the Dolphins from Brisbane this year and has had a career-best season under head coach Kristian Woolf.

He took on board advice from Maroons coach Slater, who gave him his debut in 2022.

"I'd been there in Origin for a couple of years but didn't play last year, which wasn't the best year for me," Cobbo said.

"I wanted to get back, so I worked really hard the whole off-season. All the extras I was doing paid off.

"As Billy says, if you work hard for it the rewards will come. He was real good throughout the camps, the staff as well.

"Just knowing I can play 80 minutes of Origin was a shock to me, but I enjoyed every moment of it."

Cobbo recently re-signed with the Dolphins until the end of 2031 after finding his feet following a disappointing 2025 at the Broncos.

"The club has done a lot for me. They told me they would bring me back to Origin, and I just want to give back to them and play good footy here for the next five years," he said.

Cobbo's fierce ball running in Origin this year would have made Inglis proud.

"He was my idol growing up, the way he played ... strong. It would have been hard defending against him," Cobbo said.

Now Cobbo is on track to cap off a great season with a recall to the Australian side under his old club coach Kevin Walters at the World Cup, which is another goal.

"It would be good to chuck on that (Australian) jersey again and play under Kevvie. I'll work hard to get back there," he said.

stories.headline: How to bet Falcons-Packers on TNF: Analysis, tips and top plays
stories.summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Falcons-Packers on "Thursday Night Football."
stories.body:
"Thursday Night Football" features the Atlanta Falcons visiting Lambeau Field to take on the Green Bay Packers. With Michael Penix Jr. healthy and slated to start, the Falcons get some stability at the quarterback position. Off to an 0-2 start, behind an offense that couldn't find any sense of rhythm with No. 3 QB Cooper Rush taking snaps, we finally get to see how coach Kevin Stefanski schemes for his two playmakers in the pass game -- Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. -- versus a Packers defense that is playing zone coverage on 70.5% of opponent dropbacks.

Now, Stefanski's call sheet will be based off the volume for running back Bijan Robinson, who is averaging 18.5 carries per game. We should see a lot of outside zone schemes (which should mirror the play-action passing game) versus a Green Bay defense allowing only 2.9 YPC (second fewest in the league) through the first two weeks.

For the Packers, quarterback Jordan Love has completed only 52.1% of his passes to start the season, but he has hit on eight explosive-play throws (20 or more yards), which ranks fifth in the league. Christian Watson is a big-play target who has scored three touchdowns through two weeks, while Matthew Golden is emerging as a go-to option. It's a committee approach in the backfield, one that lacks difference-making ability.

Betting outlook

Looking at a line that has dropped to Green Bay -4.5, I'm going to take the Packers to cover the spread (and a moneyline bet), plus I'm hitting the over at 42.5. I like Love and the Green Bay pass game against a Falcons defense that struggled in Week 2 versus the Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young (287 yards, three touchdowns). Expect more rhythm throws to the middle of the field, plus the isolation shots to Watson. And I think Green Bay can get enough out of this makeshift backfield (Kaleb Johnson flashed on tape last week) to sustain and control tempo. Plus, I'm betting on that Packers defense to win enough early-down situations to keep the Falcons' offense off schedule based on the game plan. We know Robinson will get his touches, and there will be schemed throws for Penix to hit based on Stefanski's history as a playcaller. But I don't think it's enough to cover or knock off the Packers at the home opener at Lambeau Field.

Total points UNDER 42.5 (-108)

Ben Solak: The Falcons finally get functional quarterback play with Penix healthy and stepping in, but he was not even an average starter when we last saw him and now takes snaps in a new offense and having seen no preseason action. I'm expecting plenty of rust against a solid Packers defense. On the other side of the ball, DC Jeff Ulbrich remains a quality designer of pressure packages -- something with which the Packers' young and injury-riddled O-line is likely to struggle. I see sacks, punts and field goals in this one.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Drake London receiving yards OVER 66.5 (-112)

I think you can bet London in this one, especially if Green Bay leans on its two-deep zone shells. This is where London can find the voids on deep-in breakers. Plus, he can win perimeter matchups when the Packers roll to man coverage.

Tucker Kraft anytime TD (+185)

If you want an anytime TD scorer? I'd take a shot on Kraft. The Packers tight end has run at least 22 routes in both games played, and he can press the seams in scoring position or see the ball off play-action in the low red zone.

Kyle Pitts Sr. receiving yards OVER 34.5 (-113)

Eric Moody: Pitts has just four targets so far this season, but with Penix under center, he should see more opportunities. He cleared this line in seven of the nine games Penix started last season while averaging 5.9 targets per game.

Matthew Golden receiving yards OVER 52.5 (-114)

Moody: Golden has seen 18 targets through two games while maintaining a high route participation rate. Green Bay's offensive line is a mess right now, and the team has struggled to run the football. That could force the Packers to lean more heavily on Love and the passing game against a Falcons defense allowing the 10th-most passing yards per game.

stories.headline: Reranking the men's basketball recruiting class of 2024
stories.summary: Cooper Flagg remains No. 1 in this high school class -- but we admit to some mistakes for the rest of the list.
stories.body:
Evaluating and projecting high school recruits is an inexact science. Talent evaluators, scouts, coaches and NBA front offices all have notable hits, along with misses. We're always looking ahead with an eye on potential. But this time, we're looking back at the top of the 2024 SC Next 100 class.

This group had some obvious stars, even at the time, such as Cooper Flagg. But there were also some less obvious risers we perhaps should've picked up on. Kon Knueppel was a productive high schooler with upside; we didn't see him taking off this quickly. The same goes for Jeremiah Fears, a five-star junior who reclassified late and, in hindsight, was slotted too low in the final player rankings.

Injuries, role changes and development can make projecting high school players especially difficult. Now, two years later, this analysis has incorporated their overall résumé to date. So, how did we do in 2024?

Note: Khaman Maluach and Egor Demin, five-star talents who would normally fit among this group, are not eligible because they played their high school basketball outside the United States.

1. Cooper Flagg, SF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 1
Flagg was different from a young age. The Maine native reclassified after his sophomore year and eventually ascended to No. 1 in the rankings, then led Montverde Academy to an undefeated season and a Chipotle Nationals championship. "He had zero ego and never complained," said Kevin Boyle Jr., Flagg's associate head coach at Montverde. "He knew when to get his teammates involved and only cared about winning." At Duke, Flagg averaged 19.2 points, 7.5 rebounds and 4.5 assists while leading the Blue Devils to the Final Four. He became just the fourth freshman to win national player of the year, before going No. 1 in the 2025 NBA draft and earning NBA Rookie of the Year honors with the Dallas Mavericks.

2. Dylan Harper, PG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 4
Harper was a productive, composed high school guard who drew comparisons to Jalen Brunson at the time with his size, production and facilitation skills. He shared MVP honors at the 2024 McDonald's All American Game before averaging 19 points as a Rutgers freshman and earning third-team All-Big Ten honors. The San Antonio Spurs selected Harper second in the draft, and he made the All-Rookie team after showing improved playmaking and scoring. In the 2026 NBA Finals, he averaged 18 points, 6.4 rebounds and three assists. Harper's strengths lie in his perimeter versatility, and he has the potential to be an All-Star at either the point guard, shooting guard or small forward position.

Previous No. 2: Ace Bailey

3. VJ Edgecombe, SG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 3
Edgecombe improved rapidly throughout high school, emerging as a dynamic transition finisher with NBA-level athleticism, scoring ability and a high basketball IQ. His explosive skills helped make him our No. 3 prospect, and he keeps the spot in these rerankings after earning second-team All-Big 12 honors during his lone season at Baylor. The Philadelphia 76ers selected Edgecombe third in the 2025 draft, and he earned first-team All-Rookie honors before becoming the youngest player in NBA history with a 30-point, 10-rebound playoff game.

4. Kon Knueppel, SG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 19
Knueppel makes one of the biggest jumps in our rerankings. His shooting and scoring ability were evident in high school: He led Wisconsin Lutheran to an undefeated season and state championship and the EYBL in scoring. Knueppel validated those strengths at Duke, earning ACC tournament MVP honors before the Charlotte Hornets selected him fourth in the draft. He made the NBA All-Rookie first team and set the sport's rookie record with 273 3-pointers. He ended up in the perfect team context and was ideally utilized which plays into his success. If not for Flagg, he would've won NBA Rookie of the Year.

Previous No. 4: Dylan Harper

5. Ace Bailey, SF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 2
Bailey was originally the second-best prospect in the 2024 class because of his enormous upside. Two years later, a few players vaulted ahead of him because they parlayed better results and ceiling. But Bailey's potential remains immense. The 6-foot-9 wing averaged 17.6 points and 7.2 rebounds at Rutgers before the Utah Jazz took him fifth in the draft. One of the youngest players in the 2025 draft class, Bailey was also the youngest player in Jazz history to score 500 career points, which helped him earn second-team NBA All-Rookie honors. His best basketball remains ahead of him.

Previous No. 5: Tre Johnson

6. Jeremiah Fears, PG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 40
Fears reclassified into the 2024 class and committed to Oklahoma in July, leaving us little time to fully evaluate his rapid development. He immediately emerged as one of the nation's most impactful freshmen, helping the Sooners reach the NCAA tournament and earning SEC All-Freshman honors. He was the No. 7 pick in the NBA draft, going to the New Orleans Pelicans. His 40-point performance against Utah on April 7 set a Pelicans rookie record and made him one of the youngest NBA players to reach the 40-point mark.

Previous No. 6: Donnie Freeman

Freeman made one of the biggest jumps of any senior in 2024, when he climbed to five-star status at the end of the cycle. He was productive over two years at Syracuse, but he has since dealt with injuries, including a torn Achilles this summer after transferring to St. John's.

7. Morez Johnson Jr., PF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 29
Johnson was a borderline five-star in high school who produced like a five-star as a dominant frontcourt player in college, giving him a significant jump from his original No. 29 spot. He had spent his freshman season at Illinois before transferring to Michigan, where he helped the Wolverines win a national championship and earned Big Ten All-Defensive honors. His sheer dominance carried into the NCAA tournament, and he became the fifth player in tournament history with a 20-point, 10-rebound game while shooting 100% from the field. Dallas selected him ninth in the 2026 NBA draft.

Previous No. 7: Ian Jackson

Jackson opened his career at North Carolina before transferring to St. John's. Expect Rick Pitino to continue to help Jackson, who has first-round upside, to develop his defense and decision-making.

8. Tre Johnson, SG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 5
Johnson was once the No. 1-ranked player in his high school class, largely because of his elite scoring ability -- and that skill has translated at every level. As a Texas freshman, he led the SEC with 20.2 points per game and earned SEC Freshman of the Year honors. The Washington Wizards took Johnson sixth in the 2025 NBA draft, and he immediately carved out a significant role, starting 42 of 60 appearances and averaging 12.2 points last season as a rookie.

Previous No. 8: Derik Queen

9. Derik Queen, C
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 8
Queen was an elite prospect early in high school and eventually finished inside the top 10 in the SC Next 100 thanks to nimble footwork, passing, soft touch and basketball IQ. After a stellar season at Maryland, he was named Big Ten Freshman of the Year, then picked 13th by the Pelicans in the 2025 draft. An elite big man passer and decision-maker, he is best when the offense plays through him. He became the first rookie center in NBA history to record a triple-double and later earned second-team All-Rookie honors.

Previous No. 9: Liam McNeeley

10. Will Riley, PF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 12
Riley intrigued us in high school because his long-term potential exceeded his production. At 6-9 with perimeter ball skills and athleticism, he possessed a compelling developmental foundation. He averaged 12.2 points at Illinois and was the Big Ten Sixth Man of the Year before Washington selected him in the 2025 draft. Last season, he averaged 10.3 points and became the first Wizards newcomer since Calbert Cheaney in 1994 to record consecutive 30-point games.

Previous No. 10: Jalil Bethea

Now at Pitt, Bethea is on his third college team in three years after dealing with a foot injury last year at Alabama. He has plenty of scoring prowess but needs to find a way to put it all together.

11. Labaron Philon Jr., PG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 32
Philon was a speedy scoring point guard who played without fear even as an underclassman, earning Alabama's Class 7A Player of the Year as a high school sophomore. He remained in-state for two seasons at Alabama and scored 725 points as a sophomore, the third most in a single season in Crimson Tide history. The Sixers drafted him 22nd in 2026. Philon gets a bump in these rerankings after taking advantage of a second college season to become a productive force and first-round pick.

Previous No. 11: Derrion Reid

Reid began his career at Alabama before transferring to Oklahoma, where he was significantly more productive as a sophomore. He returns for his junior season looking to elevate the Sooners and solidify his draft stock.

12. Carter Bryant, PF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 20
Bryant checked a lot of boxes as a five-star recruit and McDonald's All-American. Even after playing as more of a sixth man at Arizona, the Spurs bet on his long-range shooting and upside to make him a 2025 lottery pick. Bryant came off the bench over 71 games as a rookie for a Spurs team that reached the 2026 NBA Finals. He's still rising, as a defense-first prospect learning how to translate his upside into consistent production. His path to becoming a glue guy on a title contender is clear.

Previous No. 12: Will Riley

13. Asa Newell, PF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 13
Want a sense of how loaded Montverde Academy was in 2024? Newell, a five-star McDonald's All-American, was the fifth option for the championship-winning team. No matter where he has played, Newell has embraced a variety of roles. He averaged 15.4 points and 6.8 rebounds and was an SEC All-Freshman at Georgia. He was the No. 23 pick in 2025 and mostly came off the bench for the Atlanta Hawks. Newell's efficient shooting -- he shot 53.8% from the floor and 38.7% from deep his rookie season -- in a limited role could help him earn even more minutes.

14. Liam McNeeley, SF
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 9
McNeeley was a proven commodity for his entire high school career. He then led UConn in scoring at 14.5 points per game, rebounded well and shot 86% from the free throw line. The net result: being named Big East Freshman of the Year. He's currently still finding his footing with the Hornets after being traded by the Phoenix Suns -- who selected him 29th in 2025 -- though he looked more confident and comfortable coming out of summer league this year.

Previous No. 14: Drake Powell

15. Drake Powell, SG
2024 SC NEXT 100 ranking: 14
The North Carolina native was a five-star in high school, and the NBA identified that upside when Atlanta drafted him 22nd in 2025, then traded him to the Brooklyn Nets. In between, Powell stayed home to become a key member of the Tar Heels' 2024-25 rotation. His defensive versatility and coachability have shown up at every stop, and we're betting his defense helps him carve out a long career in the pros.

Previous No. 15: Isaiah Evans

stories.headline: Chloe Bibby's rollercoaster year has her ready for WNBA playoffs
stories.summary: A rollercoaster season will reach another peak for Chloe Bibby when the WNBA playoffs begin this weekend.
stories.body:
A rollercoaster season will reach another peak for Chloe Bibby when the WNBA playoffs begin this weekend.

In April, the 28-year-old Australian Opal was selected by new franchise Portland Fire in the expansion draft. Tthe following month she was traded to Phoenix Mercury then waived two days later due to a niggling knee injury.

The athletic forward with a penchant for the three-ball returned to Australia and spent time with her family in the regional Victorian city of Ballarat before earning a deal with Chicago then weeks later landing a rest-of-season contract with Minnesota Lynx who will finish the regular season as top seed.

"It's obviously been a whirlwind but an exciting one, the one that you want," Bibby told ESPN from the United States on Thursday.

"After the early setbacks, the first goal was to get back over to America. Having a month in Chicago was all awesome, everything was great, I really didn't expect the top team to then say 'Hey, come over here!'

"My career has been about staying ready and whenever I get an opportunity to go out there and give it a crack I've never left anything out there. I've always had that mentality from the jump, it comes naturally and I'm always ready and have got into that rhythm. I'm always grateful to be here but I also have the confidence in myself and my ability."

Bibby is one of eight Aussies involved in the postseason alongside Isobel Borlase (Atlanta Dream), Alanna Smith (Dallas Wings), Miela Sowah (Golden State Valkyries), Steph Talbot (Las Vegas Aces), New York Liberty pair Anneli Maley and Bec Allen and Washington Mystics' Georgia Amoore.

The only team without an Aussie suited up will be the Indiana Fever but the links are still strong with former Opal Tully Bevilaqua on the coaching staff.

Even before the playoffs begin, Bibby has already experienced quite the month.

Earlier in September, she represented the Opals at the FIBA World Cup in Germany where she played in a major tournament for Australia. In a campaign plagued by injury, to Alanna Smith and Ezi Magbegor, illness also hit the squad with several players including Bibby struck down.

On Wednesday, she posted a WNBA-career high 15 points, including five triples, when she was injected into Minnesota's game against the Fever, who Bibby played for in 2025.

"We didn't start the game great and used the opportunity to give the starters a rest but that was a lot of fun for me to have a crack, get out there and show what I can do," she said.

"It was also great to do it in front of my parents, they haven't seen me play in America before in the W so it was cool to have them there for that."

A 32-win regular campaign has the Lynx top of the league and striving for the title that eluded them in 2024 against a Sandy Brondello-coached New York Liberty.

Minnesota's last title came in 2017. In 2026, they are being paced by superstar rookie Olivia Miles, who is eighth in the league for scoring with 19.8 points per game, Kayla McBride (averaging 17.5 points, 3 rebounds and 2.2 assists) and Napheesa Collier fresh from the USA's World Cup triumph.

"It's a great team, there's Olivia Miles, the talent is crazy and the shotmaking is off the charts. It's a lot of fun to be a part of, fun to watch and I think that's what makes it so exciting and the playoff run so exciting," Bibby explained.

"Every team is so deep and has so much talent, the skills and shotmaking ability with the efficiency is crazy. I think one through eight, all the playoff games are going to be tough, next level and it's really exciting for the W.

"I think the year I've had and with everything that's happened, to win a championship would be insane and really top it off. I'm excited for all of it. Last year, when I was with the Fever, I was injured so I'm happy to be here and healthy."

The WNBA's first round and semifinals are a best-of-three format before a seven-game Finals series, to determine the 2026 champion, beginning on October 17.
